newsitem.title: USA: San Diego, California, could lose Super Bowl - League.
newsitem.headline: San Diego, California, could lose Super Bowl - League.

text.p: The National Football League said on Thursday it adopted a contingency plan to hold the 1998 Super Bowl at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena, Calif., because of a legal battle over San Diego's stadium project.

The league said it has entered into an option agreement with the Los Angeles Sports & Entertainment Commission and the Rose Bowl Operating Co to host the game in Pasadena should bonds needed to renovate San Diego's Jack Murphy Stadium be subject to a voter referendum this spring.

A trial date has been set for February 20 on San Diego's $78 million expansion and renovation of Jack Murphy stadium. Opponents of the expansion plan are demanding that San Diego place the project on the ballot.

If it becomes necessary later this month to move the Super Bowl from San Diego's stadium, the NFL said it would notify Los Angeles and Pasadena officials to begin immediate preparations to host the game.
